content:
This week, Apple announced that iOS 27 will be officially released to all users on Monday, September 14.

Additionally, the company now says that two features included in the iOS 27 beta have been removed and will be released later through a "future software update" on iPhone: suggested features in Messages, and the automatic password changing feature.

Apple updated its website this week to reflect that the aforementioned features have been temporarily pulled from iOS 27. The change also applies to other platforms, including iPadOS 27 and macOS 27. Reddit users previously noticed that the automatic password changing feature was removed in iOS 27 beta 5, and Apple has now updated its website to confirm this change.

As a reminder, the suggested feature in Messages allows users to add related items to Reminders, Notes, or Calendar with a single tap based on the content of their conversations.

Below is Apple's description of the password feature:

"The Passwords app will try to go directly to websites where your passwords are weak or have been compromised, and automatically update them for you. At WWDC, Apple explained that this feature would use Apple Intelligence and Safari to "act as an agent on your behalf".

As for when the two features mentioned above will return to iOS 27, there are no more details at the moment. Apple's website only states that they will be released in a "future software update".
